**Answer Explanation**

Let the coordinates of the unit cubes be \((x,y,z)\) with  
\(0\le x,y,z\le 2N\).  
For any \(2\times2\times2\) block the eight cubes have the same parity
pattern of the sum \(x+y+z\).  
Consequently, in a checker‑board colouring (black when \(x+y+z\) is even,
white otherwise) every such block contains exactly four black cubes,
which meets the condition “at most 4 black cubes”.

The checker‑board uses all cubes whose coordinate sum is even.
Because the whole cube has odd side length \(2N+1\), the numbers of
even‑sum and odd‑sum cubes differ by one; the even‑sum cubes are the
majority.  Hence the maximum possible number of black cubes is the
majority count:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{total cubes} &= (2N+1)^3 = 8N^{3}+12N^{2}+6N+1,\\[2pt]
\text{maximum black} &= \Big\lceil\frac{(2N+1)^3}{2}\Big\rceil
                     = \frac{(2N+1)^3+1}{2} \\
                     &= 4N^{3}+6N^{2}+3N+1 .
\end{aligned}
\]

No configuration can exceed this bound: each \(2\times2\times2\) block
contains at most half of its cubes black, and a standard averaging
argument over all such blocks yields the same global density limit of
\(1/2\).  The checker‑board construction shows the bound is attainable.

\[
\boxed{\,4N^{3}+6N^{2}+3N+1\,}
\]

**ANSWER:** 4N³ + 6N² + 3N + 1
